questions.question: Mishti's birthday is on Thursday 27th April. On what day of the week will be Aradhya's Birthday in the same year, if Aradhya was born on 20th October?
questions.solution:
Misthi’s birthday = 27th April → Thursday

Aradhya’s birthday = 20th October

Number of days between 28th April to 20th October:

Days left in April = 3

May = 31

June = 30

July = 31

August = 31

September = 30

October = 20

Total days = 176

Number of odd days = 176/7 → 1

So, Aradhya’s birthday will be on Thursday + 1 day = Friday.

Hence, the answer is Friday.

questions.question: In a row, there are 6 boys between A and B and A being the first boy in row. There are 3 boys between B and C. If there are 12 boys after C, then how many maximum boys are there in the row?
questions.solution:
A’s position = 1st

B’s position = (A + 6 *between* + B) → 8th

C’s position = (B + 3 between + C) → 12th

Number of maximum boys = 12 (C’s position) + 12 (after C)

= 24

**Alternate method:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9cf56b77b52cff6eb81c4efbae3ee26327d3e7600200ae11ea64fbed8c9d9d10.png]

questions.question: Six year ago, Parvez’s age was same as the present age of Manish. If the present age of Parvez is one-fourth more than that of Manish's present age, then in how many years will Parvez’s age become double of Manish’s present age?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of Manish and Parvez be 'M' and 'P' respectively.

As per Question: Six year ago, Parvez’s age was same as the present age of Manish

Therefore, P - 6 = M → P - M = 6 ----(1)

Again, the present age of Parvez is one-fourth more than that of Manish's present age

Therefore, P = (1/4 × M) + M → P = 5M/4 ---- (2)

From (1) and (2)

P = 30 and M = 24

Therefore Present age of Parvez and Manish is 30 and 24 respectively.

Now, if we double the present age of Manish = 24 × 2 = 48

So Parvez will be of 48 years after = 48 - 30 = 18 Years

Hence, the correct answer is 18 Years.

questions.question: If 14 (16) 18 and 33 (64) 25, then what is the value of ‘A’ in 25 (49) A?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

14 (16) 18

→ (18 - 14)² = (4)² = 16

33 (64) 25

→ (33 - 25)² = (8)² = 64

Similarly,

25 (49) A

→ (25 - A)² = (7)² or (A - 25)² = (7)²

→ 25 - 7 or 25 + 7

→ 18 or 32

Hence, the answer will be either ‘18 or 32’.

questions.question: Oxide of which of the following will turn red litmus blue?
questions.solution:
Litmus is a water-soluble mixture of different dyes extracted from lichens. It is often absorbed onto filter paper to produce one of the oldest forms of pH indicator, used to test materials for acidity.

Concept:

Metals react with oxygen to form metallic oxides.

These metallic oxides are basic in nature

Metal + Oxygen → Metallic oxide

Example:

When magnesium burns in air it combines with the oxygen of the air to form magnesium oxide

2 Mg + O2 → 2 MgO

Magnesium oxide dissolves in water to form magnesium hydroxide solution

MgO + H2O → Mg(OH)2

Magnesium hydroxide turns red litmus blue which shows its basic nature.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution prohibits trafficking, forced labour, and children working under 14 years of age?
questions.solution:
Right to Equality

 
 
 
 Government shall not deny to any person in India equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. It means that the laws apply in the same manner to all, regardless of a person's status.

 
 
 

 
 
Right to Freedom

 
 
 
 Article 19 'everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression; this right includes freedom to hold opinions without interference.

 
 
 

 
 
Right against Exploitation

 
 
 
 The Rights against Exploitation is provided under Articles 23 and 24 of the Constitution of India. The right against exploitation prohibits all forms of forced labour, child labour and trafficking of human beings.

 
 
 

 
 
Right to Freedom of Religion

 
 
 
 Freedom of religion is a fundamental right in Article 25-28 of the Constitution of India. Article 25 of Indian Constitution grants freedom to every citizen of India to profess, practice and propagate his own religion.

questions.question: Land covers about ________ of the earth's surface.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29%**__.

__
 
• About **29%** of the Earth's surface is covered by Land.
 
• About 71% of the Earth’s surface is water-covered and the **oceans hold for about 96.5%** of all Earth’s water.
 
• Water also exists in the air as water vapor in rivers and lakes, ice caps and glaciers, and in the ground as soil moisture.
 
• **Desert acquires 33% or 1/3rd of the Land Surface.**

 
 

 Components__
 __Important information__
 
 

 Lithosphere
 
 
It is the outer part of the Earth and other celestial bodies. It covers the rocky part of the body. On Earth, it is considered as the crust and the rigid upper mantle part.

 
 
 

 Hydrosphere
 It is the component of the Earth which covers about 70% of the surface. It includes the oceans, seas, lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams. 
 
 

 Biosphere
 It is the ecosystem that contains all the living beings and their relationship with nature. The term "Biosphere" was coined by geologist Eduard Suess in 1875. 
 
 

 Atmosphere
 It is kind of a blanket that contains gases and surrounds the Earth from outside. Where we live, we breathe, we act and we do daily activities are all part of the atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the area (in sq cm) of a rectangle, if its diagonal is 25 cm and one of its sides is 24 cm?
questions.solution:
Let the other side be x cm.

Length of diagonal = √(x² + 24²) cm = 25 cm

⇒ x² + 24² = 25²

⇒ x² = 625 – 576 = 49

⇒ x = 7

∴ Area of the rectangle = 7 cm × 24 cm = 168 cm²

questions.question: What is the value of tan 6° tan 36° tan 84° tan 54° tan 45°?
questions.solution:
**Formulae Used:**

tan (90° - A°) = cot A

cot A = 1/tan A

**Calculation:**

tan 6° tan 36° tan 84° tan 54° tan 45°

= tan 6° tan 36° tan (90 - 6)° tan (90 – 36)° tan 45°

= tan 6° tan 36° cot 6° cot 36° tan 45°

= tan 6° × tan 36° × (1)/(tan 6) × (1)/(tan 36) × tan 45°

= 1

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (-1, 3) in the line x = -4?
questions.solution:
Let the reflected point be (x, y).

Then the midpoint of (-1, 3) and (x, y) i.e. [(x-1)/2, (y+3)/2] must lie on the line x = -4.

⇒ (x – 1) / 2 = -4

⇒ x = -8 + 1 = -7

Since the line joining the original and the reflected point in perpendicular to x = -4, hence its slope will be equal to 0.

⇒ [y – 3]/[(-7) – (-1)] = 0

⇒ y – 3 = 0

⇒ y = 3

∴ The reflected point is (-7, 3).

questions.question: PQ is the chord of a circle whose centre is O. ROS is a line segment originating from a point R on the circle that intersect PQ produced at point S such that QS = OR. If ∠QSR = 30°, then what is the value (in degrees)of POR?

In triangle POQ,

OP = OQ (both are radius)

questions.question: A man travelled a distance of 60 km in 7 hours. He travelled partly on foot @ 6 km/hr and partly on bicycle @ 12 km/hr. What is the distance (in kms) travelled on foot?

questions.question: What is the sum of the first 11 terms of an arithmetic progression if the 4th term is 11 and the 7th term is -4?
questions.solution:
Let the first term be a and the common difference be r.

a₄ = a + (4 – 1) r

⇒ a + 3r = 11 ------ (1)

a₇ = a + (7 – 1) r 

⇒ a + 6r = -4 ------ (2)

Subtracting (1) from (2), we get

3r = -15

r = -5

a = 11 – 3 × (-5) = 26

Sum of first 11 terms = 11/2 [2 × 26 + (11 – 1) × (-5)] = 11

**∴ The sum of the first 11 term is 11**

questions.question: D and E are points on side AB and AC of ΔABC. DE is parallel to BC. If AD : DB = 2 : 5 and area of ΔABC is 98 cm sq, what is the area (in sq cm) of quadrilateral BDEC?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**AD : DB = 2 : 5

So, AB = 7a

Area of ΔABC = 7²a

⇒ 7²a = 98 

⇒ a = 2

Area of quad BDEC = 7²a - 2²a

= 45a

= 90

**__Solution:__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/618ae136594100412bd26040eca5c715a4f106c3ebfd49ffe84050e1e6ef4b5f.png] 

Since DE is parallel to BC.

⇒ ∠ABP = ∠ADQ ---- (1)

AD : DB = 2 : 5

⇒ DB/AD = 5/2

⇒ 1 + DB/AD = 1 + 5/2

⇒ (AD + DB)/AD = 7/2

⇒ AB/AD = 7/2 ---- (2)

In ΔABC and ΔADE

∠BAC = ∠DAE (common angle)

∠ABC = ∠ADE (corresponding angles) {using (1)}

∠ACB = ∠AED (corresponding angles)

⇒ ΔABC ~ ΔADE (by AAA)

⇒ AB/AD = BC/DE = 7/2 {using (2)}

⇒ DE = 2BC/7 ---- (3)

In ΔABP and ΔADQ

∠BAP = ∠DAQ (common angle)

∠ABC = ∠ADE (corresponding angles) {using (1)}

∠APB = ∠AQD = 90ᵒ

⇒ ΔABP ~ ΔADQ (by AAA)

⇒ AB/AD = AQ/AP = 7/2 {using (2)}

⇒ AQ = 2AP/7 ---- (4)

Area of ΔABC = 98 cm²

Area of ΔADE = 1/2 × DE × AQ = 1/2 × 2BC/7 × 2AP/7 = 4/49 × 1/2 × BC × AP = 4/49 × Area of ΔABC = 4/49 × 98 cm² = 8 cm²

∴ Area of BDEC = 98 – 8 cm² = 90 cm²

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

She asked Ravi, "What is worrying you?"

options.text: She asked Ravi what is worrying him.
She asks Ravi what has worrying him.
She asks Ravi what is worrying him.
She asked Ravi what was worrying him.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is __**She asked Ravi what was worrying him.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• Let's look at the steps for changing the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• As the reporting verb is in the past tense and direct speech is in the present continuous tense, we will take the following steps:-
 
 
• The reporting verb 'said' is changed to 'asked' because 'Reporting verbs such as said/ said to changes to enquired, asked, or demanded'.
 
• The conjunction 'that' is not used because 'No conjunction is used, if a sentence in direct speech begins with a question (what/where/when) as the "question-word" itself acts as a joining clause'.
 
• For Example:-
 
• Direct: “Where do you live?”, asked the boy.
 
• Indirect: The boy enquired where I lived.
 
• The present continuous tense (are going) is changed to past continuous tense (was going) in the direct speech.
 
• The pronoun 'You' is changed to 'him' according to the subject.
 
 
 
• **Thus, the sentence becomes: ***She asked Ravi what was worrying him.*

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The following table will enable us to know how tense changes in indirect speech:-

 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Simple Present* (Subject + V1 + Object)*
 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 
 

 Present Continuous *(Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Present Perfect *(Subject + has/have + V3 + Object)*
 Past Perfect* (Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 Past Perfect *(Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Perfect Continuous* (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Future *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object)*
 Present Conditional *(Subject + would + V1 +Object)*
 
 

 Future Continuous *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Conditional Continuous *(Subject + would + be + V1 + ing + Object)*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Rituals play into the __________ understandings of a society.
questions.solution:
It can be clearly apprehended that the blank requires an adjective to clearly explain the succeeding word. Since the options 1 and 4 are adverbs, they can be eliminated as an answer. 

‘Tacit’ and ‘taciturn’ are both adjectives but are different in meaning even though they seem similar. ‘Tacit’ means something understood without even being stated while ‘taciturn’ means inability of a person to speak. Here, according to the context, ’tacit’ is the most appropriate word and hence, the correct option.
